title: Farah and the River That Argued
logline: Farah fights Wisal until they discover they were always the same water.
story: Certain they were opposites and enemies, Farah, who carried joy, ran headlong against Wisal, who was union with the beloved. Each tried to push the other back uphill, and they struggled until both were spent and still. In that stillness Farah noticed they had pooled together and could no longer tell which water had been which. What Farah had fought so hard in Wisal was only the part of Farah that had never been lived. Joined, they became a river wide enough to carry them both.
moral: What you fight hardest in another is most often the unlived part of yourself.
